topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening outlines the learning objectives and frames the overall scope of the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities along with the systemic toxicity and drug resistance mechanisms that limit cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities and intrinsic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that selectively target intrinsic cellular defects such as hormone dependency, checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair mutations.

topics.label: Kinase oncogene targeting and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the design, clinical application, and resistance pathways associated with small-molecule inhibitors targeting oncogenically activated kinases.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the use of engineered antibodies to inhibit surface signaling pathways or deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapeutic strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the basis for immune surveillance against tumors and explore therapies that engage or re-engineer immune cells to destroy cancer.

topics.label: Overall progress, systemic challenges, and future directions in cancer care
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate historical progress in cancer survival alongside persistent clinical challenges and emerging paradigms for future patient management.
